description:
# Phase outcome

Jido ships as one target-specific package that contains a private Erlang/OTP runtime. The package provides the TUI, `run`, `eval`, and the optional foreground daemon. Native release jobs publish tested archives, metadata, checksums, and notices. The distribution channels use the same command and version contract.

# Entry gate

Start this phase after the current coding-pack and deterministic-automation terminal stories are complete: `jido_cli-tqg.5.7`, `jido_cli-tqg.6.2`, and `jido_cli-tqg.6.4`.

# Decision gates

- Define daemon protocol v1 before transport implementation.
- Run one bounded Burrito spike before package implementation.
- Keep only Burrito or the custom Mix release fallback after the spike.
- Pass the first native target matrix before service and distribution hardening.

# Source

Use `RELEASE_PLAN.md` as the product and release contract. If a task must change that contract, update the document in the same task and record the decision.

# Status rule

All child tasks remain open. Dependency links control implementation order. Manual TUI checks are release gates. They are not substitutes for deterministic automated checks.
title: Phase 6: Ship isolated cross-platform Jido releases
